content.title: About
content.content: Fava beans (also known as broad beans) are a legume native to the Mediterranean, North Africa and parts of Asia. Cooked fava beans have a mild, slightly nutty flavor and a tender yet firm texture. They are used in salads, spreads, soups, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fava beans are also called "broad beans" or "horse beans" in different regions.
In ancient Greek mythology fava symbolized fertility and abundance.
The seeds are protein‑rich, containing up to 26 % protein by dry weight.
In Italy, a traditional dish called "fave" is a simple puree of cooked fava beans.
Their dense texture makes them a popular meat substitute in vegetarian recipes.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Cooked fava beans provide about 7 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Fava beans supply folate, thiamine and vitamin B6, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals: iron and magnesium
items.content: Iron supports oxygen transport, while magnesium is essential for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Fava beans raise blood glucose slowly, making them suitable for blood‑sugar management.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fava beans, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and cooking help lower its level.

items.title: Raw bean toxins
items.content: Raw fava beans contain lectins that can be toxic; thorough cooking eliminates them.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook fava beans in salted water for 20‑30 minutes, then add them to salads, pastas, soups, or mash them into a spread. They pair well with olive oil, lemon, garlic, and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fava beans in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Discard any beans with off‑odors or signs of spoilage.
